name: resilient-dual-doorway-delivery
handle: resiliency-epic + doorway-federation: two doorways routing p2p-hosted landing + lamad-epr apps, resilience visible on UI
title: Both doorways (alpha.elohim.host facilitating/projection + elohim.host apex) deliver the p2p-hosted elohim-protocol landing and lamad EPR apps through the federated substrate, degrade gracefully when a backend peer is missing rows/bytes, and the resilience posture is visible to a human on the UI

vision_quotes.text: Substrate = attested. N independent replicas held by people with skin in the game; the durability contract is notarized and auditable (you can verify your data is held, not trust a promise); a reciprocity-imbalance signal fires the moment a holder lapses. Verifiable durability beats claimed durability.

For a human staring at their screen ... the substrate's claim has to show up somewhere they can see it. Not in a settings panel six clicks deep. Not as an opt-in advanced view. At the top level of the storage / compute surface, glanceable in a second.
vision_quotes.source: genesis/docs/content/elohim-protocol/resilience/README.md Part V 'The Top-Level Surface — A Bar That Tells the Truth'

vision_quotes.text: Project a single Matthew-stewarded landing-page EPR (elohim-host-landing ContentNode) through two federated doorways — alpha.elohim.host (doorway-A) and elohim.host (doorway-B / apex) ... so visiting either surface renders the elohim-app browser bundle from a single content-addressed blob.
Cross-doorway content delivery is the visible proof that the substrate, not any gateway, holds the content.

plan_deliverables.text: GET https://alpha.elohim.host/ renders the elohim-protocol landing (200, html); GET https://alpha.elohim.host/lamad renders the Lamad LMS (200, html).
GET https://elohim.host/ and /lamad render the same surfaces through doorway-B from the same content-addressed substrate.

plan_deliverables.text: A doorway whose primary storage backend lacks projection rows populates its EPR router from the configured storage pool (the federated fallback the /db route registry already uses) instead of silently serving an empty router; degraded state logs at visible level.

plan_deliverables.text: The storage apps-resolver heals a locally-missing app ZIP blob via the same T17 peer race-fetch the /blob route uses (peer_blob_inventory -> race_fetch -> finalize_fetch_success incl. serve-blob REA event), instead of 404 'App ZIP blob not found'.

plan_deliverables.text: The resilience posture is reachable by a human on the deployed surfaces: nav links to /shefa/cluster and /shefa/peers exist (today URL-only), and the steward-count/protection state for content (already live in ResilienceService + EprRelationshipCard + content-viewer Network tab + /api/v1/resilience/{id}) is discoverable, not buried.
plan_deliverables.source: 2026-05-29-durability-topology-felt-resilience.md 'Three gaps' #1 connective tissue; resilience/README.md Part V roadmap items 3

manifesto_anchors.why: Resilience is not a feature, it is the substrate posture: a federation pair that goes dark when one peer misses rows has re-created web2's single-origin failure. The doorway consulting its pool IS mutual aid expressed at the gateway layer.

Verifiable durability beats claimed durability — the substrate already heals blobs on the /blob path and books a serve-blob REA event; the apps path 404ing instead is the substrate failing to keep its own promise on the surface a human actually visits.
The epic's Part V: the claim has to show up somewhere the human can see it. alpha was serving 404s for days with protectionStatus 'at-risk' sitting unread in an API nobody surfaces.

scenarios_missing.intent: A doorway whose primary storage returns zero projection rows for its DOORWAY_ID populates its EPR router from a pool peer and serves / + /lamad; the degraded-primary state is observable.
An app whose ZIP blob is locally missing on the serving peer heals on first request via peer race-fetch and serves 200; a serve-blob REA event is booked for the source peer.
